albuterol.t: Doses of the related beta 2 -agonist albuterol, when administered intravenously, have been reported to aggravate preexisting diabetes mellitus and ketoacidosis.

glucose.t: Clinically significant changes in serum potassium and blood glucose were infrequent during clinical studies with long-term administration of Formoterol Fumarate Inhalation Solution at the recommended dose.

cortico.t: 4 CONTRAINDICATIONS Use of a LABA, including formoterol fumarate, without an inhaled corticosteroid is contraindicated in patients with asthma [ see WARNINGS and PRECAUTIONS ( 5.1 ) ] .

kspare.t: Xanthine derivatives, steroids, diuretics, or non-potassium sparing diuretics may potentiate hypokalemia or ECG changes.

7.3 Non-potassium Sparing Diuretics The ECG changes and/or hypokalemia that may result from the administration of non-potassium sparing diuretics (such as loop or thiazide diuretics) can be acutely worsened by beta-agonists, especially when the recommended dose of the beta-agonist is exceeded.

tca.t: MAO inhibitors, tricyclic antidepressants and drugs that prolong QTc interval may potentiate effect on the cardiovascular system.

7.4 MAO Inhibitors, Tricyclic Antidepressants, QTc Prolonging Drugs Formoterol, as with other beta 2 -agonists, should be administered with extreme caution to patients being treated with monoamine oxidase inhibitors, tricyclic antidepressants, or drugs known to prolong the QTc interval because the effect of adrenergic agonists on the cardiovascular system may be potentiated by these agents.

bb.t: In this setting, cardioselective beta-blockers could be considered, although they should be administered with caution.
